newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana further eases exchange controls.
newsitem.headline: Botswana further eases exchange controls.

text.p: The Bank of Botswana on Tuesday announced a further easing of exchange controls in line with the government's policy of deregulating the financial sector.

The bank said in a statement it would immediately raise the limits on onshore foreign currency accounts, offshore institutional portfolio investment, investment overseas by companies and lending to foreign non-resident controlled companies.
The bank also said it planned to introduce Bureaux de Change branches as an alternative to foreign exchange counters at commercial banks.

"It is the intention of government to encourage a greater number of players in the provision of services for the buying and selling of foreign currency and on the spot exchange with the pula," the bank statement said.

Foreign currency accounts can now be opened to a maximum of one million pula ($3.5 million) for individual accounts and 10 million pula for companies. Previous limits were 100,000 pula for individuals and one million pula for companies.
"This will facilitate foreign payments," the bank said, adding that the move would cut transaction costs and provide a currency hedge.
Currently, no resident company nor individual is allowed to open an offshore account without prior permission from the central bank.
The limit on the proportion of total investment by a financial institution that can be held offshore has been raised to 70 percent from 65 percent.
"This gives institutional investors greater freedom to make optimal investment decisions," the bank said.

Non-resident controlled companies can also now borrow up to a 4:1 debt to equity ratio without prior authority, while the amount borrowed before any capital has been brought into the country has been doubled to one million pula.

Resident-controlled companies can now also invest up to 10 million pula annually in overseas ventures. There is no change in the 100,000 pula per annum limit on individual offshore investment. ($ = 0.2805 pula)
